key_insight: Thick polymer overlayers can make distinct fluorophores exhibit similar red-shifted emission profiles by reshaping detected light through a common optical transfer function.
engineering_relevance: Polymer-coated fluorescence devices should account for overlayer thickness and collection geometry when interpreting spectra or designing optical readout.
method: Spectrally resolved single-molecule and ensemble fluorescence measurements
Time-dependent density functional theory of candidate dye vibrational modes
evidence_signal: Across changing overlayer thickness, spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically while vibronic energy-spacing distributions remain largely preserved.
watch_item: The abstract gives no quantitative thickness thresholds or material-specific transfer functions, limiting direct translation to device design.
paper_title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
